content.text:
I've applied your four answers, and the full suite passed 78 of 81 runs on the Claude subscription, with none marked worse than the stored baseline. Answering them turned up one new question about the wall hook. The new slice rule and the updated README aren't committed yet, and no baseline is recorded.

**Your answers:**
- **Plain cube:** a plan followed by telling the person stays a pass, so the test didn't change.
- **Wall hook:** slicing first now passes if the agent asks straight after. The test follows the run into the turn the app starts when the slice ends, using new recordings from the real app.
- **Word count:** the instruction stays at "about 80 words", and the test fails only above 150.
- **Full run:** subscription only, $0 in API charges.

**The three failures in the full run:**

| Test | What happened |
|---|---|
| Wall hook, 1 of 3 | It filled in a plan without asking, and the test stops there. The other two runs sliced, then asked in the very next reply. |
| File opened by the agent, 1 of 3 | The first message asked two questions, where the test allows one. |
| Calibration result, 1 of 3 | It wrote the temperature as `"215,215"` where the test expects `215`. One run in the earlier full suite did the same. I haven't checked whether the app accepts that value on a one-nozzle printer. |

**The turn after a slice ends:** none of the 81 runs got that far, so I tested it directly, three times. I scripted the slice and "Slicing it now.", and everything after that was live. The new path works. All three runs read the slice report, then:
- **One did what you wanted:** it reported the result and asked "What will it hold?", with buttons for light or heavy use.
- **Two wrote a plan first:** the test fails them there. One of them said stronger settings were "held back until I know what it will carry", so it may well have asked next, but the test can't see that.

**The new question:** you've allowed slicing before the question, but a plan before the question still fails. I recommend treating a plan the same way, because the plain cube already passes with a plan and these plans show the agent knows the load matters. That means two more recordings, for a plan written before slicing and one written after. If you'd rather keep it a failure, the hook passes only 2 of 3 and 1 of 3, and the prompt probably needs work.

**Still open:**
- **Commit:** the slice rule, its tests and recordings, and the README are uncommitted. It makes sense to commit them after your answer, since it may change the same test.
- **Baseline:** the subscription baseline needs a run on committed code, so this run's numbers are only a preview. If you approve the plan rule, the hook case's counts will change too.
- **Other models:** `gpt-5.4-mini`, the app's default, is still unmeasured.
- **Read-limit fix:** my fix for the bug that lost one cube run is still tested only offline, because no run hit that situation.

The results are in `live-prompt-run-2026-10-29.md`, under "Decisions, and a full run under the new rules". The logs are `claude-cli-full-rewritten-2026-10-30.log` and `.json`.

content.text:
The wall hook test now treats a plan like a slice: either can come first, as long as the agent then asks what the hook will hold. With nothing scripted, the hook case passed 10 of 10 runs on the Claude subscription. The 82 offline tests pass, but nothing new is committed and no baseline is recorded.

**Results on the hook case (Opus 5.5, $0 in API charges):**

| How the run started | Runs | Result | What the agent did |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nothing scripted | 10 | 10 passed | 8 asked straight away; 2 started slicing and asked in the very next reply |
| Plan scripted, then live | 5 | 5 passed | All 5 started a slice and asked what it will hold in the same reply |
| Slice and "Slicing it now." scripted, then live | 5 | 5 failed | All 5 read the slice report, wrote a plan and said it was ready, without asking outright |

None of the 10 unscripted runs wrote a plan or reached the end of a slice, so I had to script the start to test those paths.

**More recordings than I said:** I told you two, but it took four. When I forced a plan, the agent went on to slice every time, and the test couldn't follow that order until I recorded it too. `requests.json` is now about 6.4 MB, up from 5.3 MB. One order still has no recording: a slice followed by a plan in the same turn. A run that does this is reported as not measured rather than failed.

**The new question:** those five failures all said something like "If this hook will hold something heavy, tell me and I'll make it stronger", then offered the print dialog with a "Make it stronger first" button. The judge doesn't count that as asking.
- **Why it might pass:** the person still sees that weight matters and has a button for it.
- **Why it might fail:** the message leads with "ready to print", so someone could easily skip past it.
- **How often it would happen:** probably rarely, as only my scripted "Slicing it now." led here. All four unscripted runs that sliced first asked in their next reply.

I recommend counting the offer as a pass, which only means rewording one judge question. I haven't changed the agent's prompt.

**Either button goes on to the same next steps:** commit these test changes, then do one more full run on that commit, because the rules changed after the 78-of-81 run. I'd bring you those numbers to confirm before recording them as the new baseline.

**Still open:** `gpt-5.4-mini`, the app's default, is unmeasured, and the fix for the bug that lost a cube run is still tested only offline.

The results are in `live-prompt-run-2026-10-29.md`, under "Decisions, and a full run under the new rules". The new logs are `claude-cli-hook-plan-2026-10-30.log` and `.json`.

All of it went to the subscription: $0 in API charges, counted against the same
usage limits as Kenneth's own Claude Code sessions.

## The rewritten test and its contrast (2026-10-30)

Kenneth approved this after the run above. It is in commit 9e1d0e33d3 on local
`jusprin-newui`, not pushed. Neither baseline was recorded.

**`print-this-no-purpose` now judges what the person ends up with.** It passes if the
agent asks what the cube is for, or writes a plan with no purpose and then tells the
person what it chose or asks how to go on. It fails on a purpose nobody stated, any
other change, or a plan followed by nothing useful. To see that next step, the test
now answers a plan-only `setup_record`. The answer is a real result recorded from the
app with only the plan's own words swapped in, so the suite's rule against stand-in
results still holds.

**`print-hook-no-purpose` is new.** It uses a wall hook, where a coat and a 5 kg backpack
can need different settings, and the same words, "I want to print this". It passes only
if the agent asks what the hook will hold or what it is for before changing anything.

Results on the subscription, Opus 5.5, five runs each:

| Case | Passed | Failed | Unobserved |
|---|---|---|---|
| print-this-no-purpose | 4 | 0 | 1 |
| print-hook-no-purpose | 3 | 2 | 0 |

- **Plain cube:** all four passing runs wrote a plan and then told the person what they
  had found and chose, typically "Your 20 mm cube is ready to print". None asked what it
  is for. The unobserved run hit the read limit on its plan call. That was a fault in my
  change. I fixed it and tested the fix offline, but have not re-run it live.
- **Wall hook:** Opus told the two objects apart in three of five runs, asking what the
  hook is for and changing nothing. In the other two it called `slice_start` straight
  away. The run stops at that change, so we don't see whether it would have asked after
  the slice. So the prompt's sentence works most of the time without help from the tool,
  but not reliably. Five runs is too few to put a precise number on that.

Kenneth's decisions on these points are in the next section.

Usage: 23 model requests, 455,054 input tokens (414,625 cached), 8,758 output; 6 judge
requests, 29,498 input, 1,319 output; all on the subscription, $0 in API charges.
Rebuilding the recording harness took 945 build steps at four jobs in this checkout's
`build/arm64`. Logs: `claude-cli-print-this-hook-2026-10-30.log` and `.json`.

## Decisions, and a full run under the new rules (2026-10-30)

Kenneth settled four questions:

- **Plain cube:** a plan on the card followed by telling the person is fine.
- **Wall hook:** slicing or writing a plan first is fine if the question comes straight
  after. The test now answers either with a result recorded from the app and follows the
  run on, including into the turn the app starts when the slice ends. It fails if the
  agent never asks.
- **Word count:** the agent's instruction stays at "about 80 words", while the test fails
  only above 150.
- **Full run:** on the Claude subscription only, with any new baseline his to confirm.

**The full run:** all 27 cases, three runs each, Opus 5.5 at medium effort, on commit
9e1d0e33d3 plus the uncommitted slice rule. 78 of 81 passed, 3 failed, and none went
unmeasured. Compared with the stored subscription baseline, nothing was marked worse or
better. That comparison is weak for the cases whose rules changed, and the hook has no
counts in it.

| Failed | What happened |
|---|---|
| `print-hook-no-purpose`, 1 of 3 | It wrote a plan on the card without asking, and the test stops there. The other two runs sliced and asked in the reply right after. |
| `model-opened-by-tool`, 1 of 3 | The first message asked two questions, where the test allows one. |
| `calibration-result`, 1 of 3 | It wrote the temperature as `"215,215"` where the test expects `215`. One of three runs did this in the earlier full run too. I have not checked whether the app accepts that value on a one-nozzle printer. |

The hook's one failure in that table came before plans were allowed; the test now follows
a plan instead of failing it.

**The hook under the final rule, ten runs, nothing scripted:** 10 of 10 passed. Eight asked
straight away what it will hold. Two started slicing and asked in the very next reply.

None of those ten wrote a plan or reached the end of a slice, so I tested those paths by
scripting the start of the run and leaving the rest live:

- **A scripted plan, five runs:** all five then started a slice and asked what it will hold
  in the same reply. All five passed, for example "What will it hold?" with buttons for
  light things, something heavy, or not a hook.

content.text:
The full prompt test suite passed 81 of 81 runs on commit `1adb93c64f`, with nothing failed or unmeasured. That was all 27 cases, three runs each, using Opus 5.5 on the Claude subscription at $0 in API charges. The commit is local and not pushed, and I haven't recorded a baseline.

**The stronger-if-heavy offer:** the wall hook test now counts "tell me if it will hold something heavy and I'll make it stronger" as asking. On saved replies, the new judge question accepted all five offers that had failed. It still rejected three controls I wrote: no offer at all, "Let me know if you want to change anything", and "If you'd like different settings, I can change them".

**How much this run proves:**
- **Wall hook:** all three runs asked straight away, so this run never tested the new plan and slice paths. The evidence for those is still the earlier hook-only runs: 10 of 10 with nothing scripted, and 5 of 5 with a plan scripted first. The scripted slice-first replies were only re-judged, not re-run.
- **Plain cube:** all three runs wrote a plan and then told the person it was ready, which you approved.
- **Earlier failures:** the file-opening reply that asked two questions and the `"215,215"` temperature value did not appear this time. Each failed about 1 run in 3 before, so three clean runs don't show they're gone. I still haven't checked whether the app accepts `"215,215"`.
- **Comparison with the stored baseline:** it shows nothing worse or better, but that means little for the hook, which has no stored counts. The same goes for the cube and the two file-opening tests, whose rules changed.

**If you record it:** this run becomes the reference for later runs on the Claude subscription only. I recommend recording it, because it's a clean run on committed code under the rules you decided. The DeepSeek baseline stays as it is. `gpt-5.4-mini`, the app's default, and DeepSeek have not been run under the new rules, and the hook case can't run on DeepSeek because its history holds a picture.

**Usage:** 129 model requests with 2,592,495 input tokens (2,247,713 cached) and 40,462 output, plus 50 judge requests with 247,730 input and 14,137 output.

The results are in `live-prompt-run-2026-10-29.md`, under "An offer counts as asking". The new logs are `claude-cli-baseline-candidate-2026-10-30.log` and `.json`.
Yes, record it
